title: Joan's trial
hookLine: the transcripts survive: asked if she was in God's grace, she answered carefully and wisely

lines: ARE YOU IN THE GRACE OF GOD?
cards: Do you know if you are in the grace of God? The question comes across a room full of churchmen in Rouen. The young woman on the bench is a prisoner, a peasant girl who led soldiers and is now on trial for her life.
The trap is plain to see. If she says yes, she claims to know what only God knows. If she says no, she has just confessed.
There is no safe answer. Her reply was taken down by the court's own notaries, and the record still survives.

teach.h: A PEASANT GIRL BEFORE A CHURCH COURT.
teach.b: Start with who she was. Joan of Arc was a peasant girl who said the voices of saints had told her to help the French king.
She went to war, she was captured, and she was handed to a church court sitting in a city under English rule. The charge was heresy; the stakes were political too. Next, the question.
Catholic teaching, as the Council of Trent later put it, holds that no one can be certain, by their own reckoning, of being in God's grace.

teach.h: A QUESTION WITH ONLY BAD ANSWERS.
teach.b: So the question had only bad answers, and it was asked to catch her. Then, her answer.

teach.h: IF I AM NOT, MAY GOD PUT ME THERE.
teach.b: As the record gives it, she said: if I am not, may God put me there; and if I am, may God keep me so. She didn't claim certainty. She didn't confess guilt.
She turned the question into a prayer and handed the answer back to God.
In Matthew's Gospel, in the Douay-Rheims, Jesus tells his disciples that when they are handed over they should "take no thought how or what to speak," because it will be given them in that hour.
Some readers hear Joan's reply as exactly that. Finally, how it ended. The court condemned her, and she was burned at Rouen.
Years later a second church inquiry declared the trial void, and in time the Church named her a saint.
A church court condemned her, and the Church later called her holy. Her careful answer outlasted the court that asked it.

how: Catholics honor Joan of Arc as a saint and one of the patron saints of France, and her trial records are still read and studied; some keep her feast with Mass and with prayers for France.

games.q: you're Joan, on the bench at Rouen. a judge asks: do you know if you are in the grace of God? what do you say?
o: if I am not, may God put me there; if I am, may God keep me so.
games.why: she claimed no certainty and confessed no guilt. she turned the trap into a prayer, and the record kept it.

practice: Let a question come that you've been dodging, like am I being fair to my brother, or is this habit hurting me, and don't grab the answer that flatters you or the one that condemns you.
Try Joan's shape: name both possibilities, and stop pretending to know more than you do. If you pray, borrow her words, may God put me there; if not, stay with the question without flinching.

wordCard.voice: Joan's trial. The church court at Rouen that questioned Joan of Arc, and the careful reply its record kept: if I am not in God's grace, may God put me there. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: may God put me there. An honest answer can also be a prayer. That's day eight hundred twenty-nine.
